chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Sa'dan ibn Muslim said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
"There is no harm in marrying a virgin if she consents, without her father's permission."

This report does not contradict what we have previously mentioned from the reports that she does not have authority alongside her father, and that whenever she contracts marriage on her own, he has the right to annul the contract, because this report implies two things: one is that this is specific to Nikah al-Mut'ah, as we mentioned regarding the concession in that regard with the conditions we cited; and the other is that it is applicable to the case where her father obstructed her and did not marry her to a suitable match, in which case it is permissible for her to contract marriage on her own.

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: If she rejects the contract, the father cannot force her, and the contract does not stand with her dislike. What I rely on in this matter is that whenever he marries her to a suitable match, she cannot oppose him, and her dislike is not taken into account.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a virgin daughter's marriage if her father arranges it without her consent?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic debate regarding a virgin's (*bikr*) autonomy in marriage by offering two reconciling interpretations: either the permission applies specifically to *Nikah al-Mut'ah* or to cases where the father obstructs a suitable match (*'adl*). Shaykh al-Tusi ultimately favors the view that a father's choice of a worthy suitor (*kuf'*) is binding on the daughter, reflecting the Shia emphasis on paternal guardianship (*wilayah*) balanced with the requirement of consent. This ruling underscores the practical implication that while a virgin's consent is necessary, it is not absolute if the father selects a compatible partner.
